channel.title: GESOFT articles
channel.description: Expert articles for business owners: processes, software and when custom IT is worth it.

item.title: Transport company software: one record for the job, the truck and the document
item.description: A dispatcher does not buy “an IT system”. They buy one truth about the haulage job, the vehicle, the driver and the document. Transport company software instead of a spreadsheet, a WhatsApp group and three versions of the freight rate.

item.title: BDO and waste records in a Polish company: KPO, KEO and a panel that does not lie at a WIOŚ inspection
item.description: You are not buying a green certificate. You are buying one waste card and a KPO that does not lie when the inspectorate arrives. Official BDO is mandatory — GESOFT does not replace it. We build the operating layer: on-site waste stock, scale, photo, handover, reminders and an export under your MOS account.

item.title: Accounting-office software: client portal, KSeF, e-Deliveries
item.description: You are not buying a VAT engine. You are buying one client file that does not vanish between mail, WhatsApp and a USB stick. Accounting-office software is a portal, a workflow and a mailbox — not another ledger.

item.title: Employment-agency software: ATS, temporary-worker records, hours, GDPR
item.description: You are not buying an ATS from the valley. You are buying one card for the candidate and the temporary worker that will survive a labour inspection and a GDPR access request. Employment-agency software instead of Excel, Telegram and three unconnected SaaS tools.

item.title: Housing-community software: advances, utilities, resolutions and a resident portal
item.description: A Polish housing community (wspólnota) is created by law, not by a spreadsheet. Software for a community ties together unit files, maintenance advances, utility billing, owner resolutions and a resident portal. Packaged SaaS is often enough. A custom system — when the process, brand or portfolio does not fit a template. Software does not replace a licensed property manager.

item.title: Housing-cooperative software: unit register, utilities, members’ portal, resolutions
item.description: A cooperative board does not buy “an IT system”. It buys one truth about the unit, the advance, the repair fund and the ticket. Housing-cooperative software instead of three spreadsheets, a caretaker’s notebook and the president’s inbox.

item.title: Association and foundation software: members, dues, OPP, a portal
item.description: A board is not looking for a generic CRM. It needs a member register, dues, a portal, and order before the AGM and the public-benefit report. Association software and foundation software — instead of Excel, a Messenger group, and three truths about the same person.

item.title: Property-manager software: defects, walk-throughs, TBS, administrator app
item.description: A community, a TBS and a tenement will not fit Excel after the fifth address. Property-manager software holds the building card, defect tickets and walk-throughs — with an administrator app in a basement with no signal.

item.title: Software for a volunteer fire brigade and a sports club: dues, timetable, kit
item.description: A volunteer fire brigade and a sports club share the same pain: a member register, dues, duty and a facility calendar. OSP and club software instead of Excel and Facebook.

item.title: Escape room booking system: rooms, slots, deposits, online tickets
item.description: An escape room sells a specific hour in a specific room. Two bookings for “Hospital 6 pm” is a disaster. An escape-room booking system, room calendar, online tickets and a deposit — instead of Messenger and Excel.

item.title: Optician and optical shop software: exams, prescriptions, frame orders
item.description: An optical shop is a clinic + stock + a workshop. The prescription, frames, lenses and pickup get lost between a notebook and the lab. Optician software: eye-test booking, a client card, order status and an SMS when the glasses are ready.

item.title: Solar and renewable-installer app: leads, installs, service
item.description: Solar, heat pumps and batteries are a funnel + a crew on a roof + a service visit in two years. A spreadsheet will not watch permits, panel deliveries and a handover protocol. A PV installer app: CRM, install schedule, a phone checklist, field service.

item.title: Speech-therapist software: booking, child cards, exercises, payments
item.description: A speech clinic lives on a course and on parents asking about progress. A notebook and a Messenger group will not watch attendance, homework and instalments. Speech-therapy software: a calendar, a child card, a parent portal, SMS, lesson packs.

item.title: Meal-prep and diet-catering software: orders, menus, delivery routes
item.description: A subscription meal box is not a 20-SKU shop. It is calorie variants, skipped days, allergens, tomorrow’s production and a courier with 40 stops. Niche tools (MasterLife CRM, x-catering, SOT) can work. A custom app — when your diet and logistics do not fit the template.

item.title: Dog groomer software: bookings, pet cards, SMS
item.description: Grooming is not a 30-minute haircut. Breed, coat and nails are 2–4 hours on the table. An online calendar, a dog card and a Saturday deposit — or Messenger and a no-show that eats the whole bay.

item.title: Tattoo studio booking system: deposit, consents, artist portfolio
item.description: A 4–8 hour session and a design the artist prepped at night. A no-show without a deposit is a whole day gone. A calendar with a deposit, a consent form and a reference photo is a studio tool, not a “nice website”.

item.title: Dietitian software: visits, meal plans, measurements, patient portal
item.description: A nutrition practice lives on a course, not a one-off consult. Spreadsheet calories and a PDF in email die on the third patient of the day. A system: calendar, card, plan, weight in an app — or the patient “lost the file” and does not return.

item.title: Physiotherapy booking system: clinic, treatment courses, home visits
item.description: Physio sells a course of 5–10 visits and a table, not “a free hour”. Patients vanish after the third session; home visits scramble the diary. A calendar with courses, rooms and travel plus SMS — instead of two Google Calendars and a WhatsApp group.

item.title: Equipment rental software: bookings, deposits, returns, damage
item.description: Skis, bikes, tools, racks, dresses, PA — the same problem: an item cannot go out twice on the same weekend. A spreadsheet will not watch deposits, service and a late return. A resource calendar with a deposit and a photo protocol.

item.title: Used-car lot software: stock, reservations, commission, contracts
item.description: A consignment lot is not a classified ad. It is a contract with the owner, a commission, a reservation with a deposit and a log of who viewed the VIN. A spreadsheet mixes “ours” with “on consignment” and will not lock a car that already has a deposit.

item.title: Soft-play and kids’ birthday booking: rooms, packages, deposits
item.description: Saturday at 3 pm is one slot, not “we will squeeze a second group”. Soft play lives on birthdays and weekends. A room calendar, a package (host, cake, hours) and a deposit — instead of Facebook and two bookings on the same room.

item.title: Dry-cleaner and laundry software: intake, status, pickup, delivery
item.description: The customer asks if the suit is ready. Staff hunt a bag by a paper number. Laundry software: intake with a photo, SMS status, pay on collection or online, a B2B pickup route — instead of a notebook and three calls a day from the same hotel.

item.title: Roadside and tow-truck app: jobs on a map, status, photos
item.description: The dispatcher is on the phone, the driver does not know which job is closer, the customer asks where you are. An app: a map pin, ETA, tow photos, payment. Android in the cab, a panel at base — not a WhatsApp group.

item.title: What Glovo, Pyszne.pl and Uber Eats commission really costs — run the numbers
item.description: Polish trade round-ups for 2026 put aggregator commissions roughly between 10–15% (pickup / own courier) and 25–35% with the platform’s rider. At 40 orders a day that is not “a few zloty” — it is a cook’s wage or the rent.

item.title: No-shows: what an empty hour costs in a salon, clinic and restaurant
item.description: Hair and beauty trade benchmarks put no-shows around 14–15% of visits, medical clinics around 18%, restaurants without a deposit often 5–20% of bookings. That is not bad luck. It is missing reminders, deposits and a waitlist.

item.title: Mandatory KSeF 2026 in a company app: who must comply and how to wire invoices
item.description: From 1 February 2026 KSeF is mandatory for large taxpayers (2024 sales over PLN 200 million gross); from 1 April 2026 for other firms. An off-the-shelf accounts tool may be enough. A custom B2B panel, CRM or wholesale system must issue a structured invoice, not a PDF in email.

item.title: Google Business Profile or your own website? What a local firm needs in 2026
item.description: A Google Business Profile is mandatory if people type “hairdresser nearby”. It does not replace a site with a calendar, a price list and a GDPR consent. Facebook is not your customer database — the algorithm can bury a post overnight.

item.title: Veterinary clinic software: patient cards, vaccines, appointments
item.description: A clinic has several animals per owner, vaccine and drug history, and bookings at 10 pm. Off-the-shelf tools (VetFile, Veterinaro, lecznica.eu) can be free at the start. A custom system makes sense when the protocol, drug stock and a second site do not fit a subscription.

item.title: Online booking system for car washes and detailing studios
item.description: A detailing bay is 2–8 hours you cannot sell twice. A Messenger queue and “I’ll drop by after work” end as an empty box and a complaint. An online calendar with a deposit and SMS guards the bay the same way it guards a salon chair.

item.title: Driving school software: course sign-up, lessons, payments, test dates
item.description: The pupil does not know how many hours are left. The instructor keeps the rota in their head. The office chases instalments. Driving-school software ties theory, yard hours and the test — instead of three spreadsheets and a Facebook group.

item.title: Nursery and kindergarten software: enrolment, attendance, fees, parent app
item.description: A parent asks the group chat whether the child ate lunch. The head chases fees in Excel. Kindergarten software collects intake, attendance and messaging — with the GDPR bar a child’s file needs.

item.title: Cleaning company app: site rotas, checklists, after photos
item.description: A crew will not fill in a spreadsheet after eight sites. A cleaning app shows today’s list, a washroom checklist and a photo after the job — the B2B client sees a report, and you see which contract still has margin.

item.title: Online ticket sales for events — without a ticketing-platform cut
item.description: Going, Eventim and peers take a cut of the ticket and keep your audience. Your own ticketing for a concert, conference, amateur match or workshop leaves the margin and an email list you have consent for.

item.title: Online booking system for local services — a calendar that works for you
item.description: Hairdresser, physio, workshop, room, advisor — the same pain: calls during work and no-shows. An online booking system takes reservations 24/7, guards resources and reminds the client before they forget.

item.title: Online table booking system for restaurants — fewer calls, more guests
item.description: A guest who cannot get through on Friday at 6 pm goes to a competitor. Your own table booking system takes reservations 24/7, cuts no-shows and puts the floor back in your hands — with no commission per seat.

item.title: Online booking system for a hair salon — no more answering the phone mid-cut
item.description: A client who cannot get through on Saturday books the competitor. An online calendar takes bookings 24/7, sends SMS reminders and tracks who is free — the stylist cuts instead of answering the phone. Fewer no-shows, more chairs earning.

item.title: QR menu and table ordering: faster service, higher bills
item.description: The guest scans a code, sees a live menu, orders and adds extras without waiting for a waiter. The kitchen gets the ticket immediately. You stop reprinting 200 menus after every price change and pay no platform cut.

item.title: Beauty salon software: bookings, treatment cards and stock
item.description: A beauty clinic lives on return visits and skin history, not a one-off appointment. Cosmetics salon software holds the client card, treatment protocol, consent and the next date — instead of a binder and one therapist’s memory. Fewer no-shows on 60–90 minute slots.

item.title: Your own restaurant online ordering system — no aggregator commission
item.description: An aggregator takes 20–30% of every order and keeps the customer in its app. Your own ordering site, payment and delivery leave the margin in the venue and build a list nobody can switch off.

item.title: Online appointment system for GP practices and clinics
item.description: Phone booking bursts in the morning and goes quiet in the afternoon. Online registration takes appointments 24/7, cuts no-shows and leaves reception time for patients who really need to call. Health data — privacy by design, not a GDPR sticker.

item.title: Workshop software: jobs, vehicle history, parts
item.description: A reception notebook and “car ready” texts do not scale past the third bay. Workshop software holds the job from check-in to invoice, VIN history and parts stock — the mechanic knows what to do and the customer stops calling every hour.

item.title: PHP application security audit: what we check before it is too late
item.description: Most leaks in small and mid-size companies come from old PHP panels that everyone knows still work. An audit is not an accusation — it is a list of risks you can close before someone uses them.

item.title: A restaurant and café loyalty programme that actually brings guests back
item.description: Paper stamp cards get lost. An aggregator app awards points to them, not you. Your own loyalty programme — points, stamps, birthday coupons — keeps the guest in your venue and gives a reason to order again.

item.title: Dental practice software: appointments, treatment plans, the chair
item.description: In dentistry an empty chair-hour hurts more than in most services. Dental software runs the diary, the treatment plan, deposits and recall reminders — so the chair earns and the patient returns. Average dental no-show sits around 12%.

item.title: Membership and class booking system for gyms and fitness clubs
item.description: A spreadsheet of check-ins breaks at peak hour. A club app shows pass validity, open spots in yoga and reminds people before the membership lapses — before they leave for a chain. Churn is won in the first 90 days, not in December.

item.title: Online booking system for hotels and guesthouses without OTA commission
item.description: Booking and Airbnb take a cut and put you next to twenty other properties. Your own booking engine on the hotel site keeps the guest with you: room calendar, deposit, seasons and a channel nobody can switch off.

item.title: CRM for law firms: matters, deadlines, time, billing
item.description: The matter in email, deadlines in Google Calendar, time in Excel, the invoice in another tool. A law-firm CRM puts the client, the matter and billable hours in one place — with the permissions professional secrecy needs.

item.title: B2B portal for wholesalers: private prices, orders, stock
item.description: The sales rep in Excel, stock in the warehouse, an order by email at 9 pm. A B2B portal lets trade customers order at their price, credit limit and live stock — no call to the office, no discount mistakes.

item.title: Property CRM and unit reservations for developers and agencies
item.description: A spreadsheet of stock is stale after the first call. A property CRM shows which units are free, reserved and sold, who owns the client and which contract stage you are in — without three truths in three files.

item.title: Field service app: jobs, visit report, van stock
item.description: Crews in the field will not fill in a spreadsheet after they get back. A technician app shows today’s jobs, navigation, a checklist and visit photos — the office sees live status, the customer gets a report without waiting for paper.
